scope_note: Daily edition from matching Friday /new listings: 107 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 36 cs.RO rows, 133 deduplicated papers, and 112 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from the repository parser output; no figure/table claims are asserted.
executive_thesis: The August 14 batch moves robotics and embodied AI toward pre-commit evidence: a robot should know when to abort before contact, when a VLA internal state signals stalled progress, when an agent must acquire another semantic-geometric view, and when a simulator or 3D representation is trustworthy enough to train or evaluate control. ContactGuard, task-progress probes, FUSE, HumanoidVLN, H2R-Bench, BrainWAM, TRAPSBench, and LocusGS all pressure the same decision boundary: before deploying a model, name the evidence that can change, stop, route, or invalidate the next action.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Monitoring has to fire before commitment
decision_cards.body: ContactGuard and VLA progress probes turn latent futures and residual streams into abort or stall signals before a contact-rich policy fails visibly.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Embodied agents must buy evidence actively
decision_cards.body: FUSE, SAP-Nav, Semantic Radiance Fields, and HumanoidVLN ask whether viewpoint choice, semantics, geometry, and embodiment physics change the executable route or interaction.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World models need transfer diagnostics
decision_cards.body: H2R-Bench, DreamX-Phi, RGB-D handover generation, and BrainWAM evaluate generated futures by embodiment correctness, functional contact, and planning-relevant action representations.

papers.title: ContactGuard: Pre-Contact Execution Monitoring with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models
papers.fit: contact-rich manipulation - latent world model - pre-contact abort signal
papers.status_quo: Many manipulation monitors discover failure after the robot has already committed to contact.
papers.friction: Wrist-camera observations reveal contact well, but a bad approach can already push, miss, slip, or disturb the object.
papers.hidden_premise: A planned action chunk can be audited in latent visual space before contact authority is granted.
papers.conceptual_move: Predict the short-horizon consequence of the policy's own action chunk and abort when the predicted post-contact latent looks unsafe.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a latent world model trained from unlabeled robot trajectories plus a small labeled pre-contact failure probe.

evidence.claim: The monitor anchors prediction before an imminent contact event and rolls forward under the policy's own actions.
It transfers to a live robot as a pre-contact abort signal without modifying the underlying policy.
APRL should score warning lead time and false aborts before final manipulation success.

papers.falsification: If aborts fire only after irreversible object motion, the model is a failure detector rather than a pre-contact monitor.
papers.adversarial: Latent prediction can reward visually common contacts; test novel object stiffness, gripper approach angle, and distractor motion.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat a planned action chunk as a hypothesis that must pass a latent future check.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for contact-rich manipulation with action chunks; weaker for black-box controllers that do not expose planned actions.

papers.title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
papers.fit: VLA interpretability - task progress probe - runtime monitoring
papers.status_quo: VLAs are approaching deployment while their internal task-state representation remains weakly instrumented.
papers.friction: A policy can appear active while internally stalled, and final success is too late to diagnose that state.
papers.hidden_premise: Task progress is encoded in activations strongly enough to be read without robot-specific labels.
papers.conceptual_move: Probe the residual stream for normalized time remaining and use the signal as a label-free OOD or stall detector.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports a linearly readable progress signal in pi_0.5 activations that generalizes to unseen tasks.

evidence.claim: A single linear probe generalizes to unseen tasks and varies under language counterfactuals when trained on multi-prompt data.
The signal is useful for detecting stalled task progress but does not enable meaningful policy steering.
APRL should separate monitoring value from steering authority when probing VLA internals.

papers.falsification: If the progress probe tracks time elapsed rather than causal task state, it will fail under pauses, detours, and recovery behaviors.
papers.adversarial: Language counterfactual sensitivity can create prompt artifacts; test physically equivalent instructions and different action horizons.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask whether an internal signal is a monitor, a control knob, or merely a clock.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for deployed VLA monitoring; weaker for policies whose internals are inaccessible or heavily quantized.

papers.title: FUSE: Active Functional Affordance Grounding through Adaptive Semantic-Geometric Evidence Acquisition
papers.fit: active affordance grounding - semantic-geometric evidence - viewpoint planning
papers.status_quo: Affordance grounding is often evaluated from fixed views that may not expose the function-relevant cue.
papers.friction: An object can satisfy a functional query only from a hidden handle, opening, support surface, or interaction region.
papers.hidden_premise: A grounded affordance answer should include the evidence-acquisition policy that made the answer possible.
papers.conceptual_move: Let the agent sequentially explore and select informative viewpoints using uncertainty-driven semantic-geometric evidence.
papers.mechanism: The abstract introduces Active Functional Affordance Grounding, FUSE, and a Habitat-based benchmark for active functional grounding.

evidence.claim: Existing methods lack mechanisms for deciding where to look when functional cues are occluded or incomplete.
FUSE combines explicit uncertainty-driven exploration with a learned amortized planner.
APRL should log which additional view changes the target mask or interaction choice.

papers.falsification: If performance comes from object identity priors rather than acquired functional evidence, the active grounding claim weakens.
papers.adversarial: Evaluate visually similar objects with different functional states and occluded affordance cues.
papers.thinking_tool: A functional affordance label is incomplete without the viewpoint path that justified it.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for object navigation and manipulation preconditions; weaker for tasks where function is visible in a single canonical view.

papers.title: HumanoidVLN: A Physics-Grounded Simulator and Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation Across Diverse Humanoid Embodiments
papers.fit: humanoid VLN - physics-grounded benchmark - embodiment variation
papers.status_quo: VLN benchmarks often assume wheeled or abstract agents that do not expose humanoid locomotion constraints.
papers.friction: A route instruction can be feasible for one body but fail under another morphology, controller, or egocentric camera motion.
papers.hidden_premise: A VLN simulator is useful only if model, controller, and embodiment failures are separable.
papers.conceptual_move: Build a physics-grounded humanoid VLN benchmark spanning multiple robot bodies, path trackers, and 3DGS reconstructed scenes.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes Isaac Sim, four humanoid configurations, hierarchical control, collision-aware episodes, and a sim-to-real pilot.

evidence.claim: The benchmark covers robots from 10-12 lower-body DoF and heights from 1.17m to 1.80m.
A 20-episode sim-to-real pilot reports strong correlation between simulation and real navigation errors.
APRL should score route following by embodiment-specific failure, not only language grounding.

papers.falsification: If failures correlate mainly with controller tuning rather than VLN reasoning, the benchmark must expose that split explicitly.
papers.adversarial: Test low-light, stairs, narrow passages, moving obstacles, and camera oscillation to separate perception from locomotion constraints.
papers.thinking_tool: Embodiment is an experimental variable, not a nuisance condition.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for humanoid navigation and mobile robotics; less direct for tabletop manipulation.

papers.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
papers.fit: human-to-robot video generation - cross-embodiment transfer - manipulation diagnostics
papers.status_quo: Human manipulation videos are abundant, but robot demonstrations remain expensive and embodiment-specific.
papers.friction: A generated robot-centric video can look plausible while failing the functional contact or embodiment constraints that matter for training.
papers.hidden_premise: Human-to-robot generation should be evaluated as transfer of task events and object responses, not video quality alone.
papers.conceptual_move: Benchmark models that transform egocentric human demonstrations into robot manipulation videos under specified embodiments.
papers.mechanism: The abstract defines annotations for task goals, action events, functional contacts, object responses, and five evaluation dimensions.

evidence.claim: The benchmark evaluates goal-state completion, action-event completion, functional contact transfer, embodiment correctness, and video quality.
It reports that current video world models often fail embodiment consistency, functional interaction, and task execution.
APRL should use generated manipulation videos only after contact and embodiment transfer tests pass.

papers.falsification: If metrics can be satisfied without improving robot policy learning, the benchmark remains a video diagnostic rather than a data asset test.
papers.adversarial: Evaluate left-right hand swaps, gripper geometry changes, hidden contact, and object dynamics that look visually plausible but are physically wrong.
papers.thinking_tool: Generated robot data needs functional contact validity before scale matters.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation data generation; weaker for tasks where human and robot embodiments share no action correspondence.

papers.title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving
papers.fit: autonomous driving VLA - world action model - action-space coordination
papers.status_quo: Driving planners often emphasize either semantic reasoning from VLMs or predictive dynamics from world models.
papers.friction: A naive shared attention space can let semantic shortcuts dominate and suppress planning-relevant predictive dynamics.
papers.hidden_premise: Semantic priors and predictive futures should coordinate at the action representation rather than compete for token attention.
papers.conceptual_move: Create specialized semantic and world-model pathways that align at compact action representations for driving control.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes action-space coordination and asynchronous rectified-flow inference with decoupled video and action denoising.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies an attention-allocation mismatch in naive VLA and WAM combination.
It reports state-of-the-art performance on NAVSIM v1 and NAVSIM v2 under the described framework.
APRL should test whether predictive dynamics changes the planned action under the same semantic scene label.

papers.falsification: If gains come from benchmark-specific priors without safer counterfactual actions, the action-space coordination claim is narrow.
papers.adversarial: Stress rare maneuvers where semantic rules and predictive motion cues disagree, then inspect which pathway controls the action.
papers.thinking_tool: Combine priors at the action contract, not only in a shared representation pool.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for driving and mobile planning; less direct for manipulation without explicit future-dynamics channels.

papers.title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
papers.fit: VLM abstention - visual uncertainty - output-stage restraint
papers.status_quo: VLMs are usually rewarded for answering, even when the visual evidence is insufficient.
papers.friction: A model can internally detect that an answer is unknowable but still output a confident response.
papers.hidden_premise: Reliability requires coupling hidden-state uncertainty to an explicit abstention interface.
papers.conceptual_move: Use matched physics video pairs where a targeted visual change makes the outcome undeterminable, then score both answers and abstentions.
papers.mechanism: The abstract introduces TRAPSBench, PECS, hidden-state answerability probes, and output-stage steering of a void direction.

evidence.claim: Across 16 VLMs, spontaneous restraint is poor and the best PECS is 0.292.
Hidden states encode answerability up to 0.91 AUROC, while outputs often fail to abstain.
APRL should require a robot VLM to abstain before approving a visually underdetermined action.

papers.falsification: If abstention improves only on synthetic physics pairs, transfer to real robot scenes with partial occlusion remains unproven.
papers.adversarial: Test uncertainty from occlusion, reflection, motion blur, and object disappearance rather than text-only impossibility.
papers.thinking_tool: A hidden uncertainty signal is not a safety feature until it changes the output contract.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLM decision gates and robot-scene QA; weaker for low-level control without language-mediated approvals.

papers.title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.fit: feed-forward 3DGS - spatial anchors - structured scene tokens
papers.status_quo: Query-based feed-forward 3DGS can decode Gaussians whose learned queries scatter across distant scene regions.
papers.friction: A latent scene token that lacks spatial coherence is hard to use as a map, object, or localization interface.
papers.hidden_premise: A 3D scene token should carry an explicit local support region rather than only a learned latent identity.
papers.conceptual_move: Augment each Gaussian query with a progressively refined 3D anchor center and support radius.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes anchor-to-ray geometric bias for evidence aggregation and anchor-centered Gaussian decoding.

evidence.claim: The authors observe that Gaussians decoded from the same query often scatter across distant scene regions.
Learned anchors form coherent spatial layouts and more structured Gaussian distributions.
APRL should evaluate whether anchored scene tokens improve localization or object retrieval under geometry corruption.

papers.falsification: If anchored tokens improve rendering but not localization, retrieval, or planning decisions, the robotics value remains indirect.
papers.adversarial: Attack with sparse views, dynamic objects, repeated structures, and missing geometry before treating anchors as map elements.
papers.thinking_tool: A 3D representation becomes robot-usable when tokens have spatial responsibility.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for map and simulator representation design; weaker for tasks that only need photorealistic novel views.

synthesis.title: Execution monitors are shifting earlier in the rollout
synthesis.facts: The papers expose latent futures, residual-stream progress, and hidden answerability before failure or overconfident output.
synthesis.inference: APRL should require every monitor to report lead time, authority, and the condition that blocks the next action.

synthesis.title: Embodied evidence is becoming actively acquired
synthesis.links: FUSE - SAP-Nav - Semantic Radiance Fields - HumanoidVLN
synthesis.facts: The batch links viewpoint selection, semantic-free-space queries, humanoid physics, and active navigation to downstream choices.
synthesis.inference: The useful benchmark records which additional observation changed target, route, contact, or stop decisions.

synthesis.title: Generated worlds need embodiment and action contracts
synthesis.links: H2R-Bench - DreamX-Phi - RGB-D handover generation - BrainWAM
synthesis.facts: The papers score human-to-robot transfer, action-conditioned futures, RGB-D handover prediction, and semantic-dynamic action coordination.
synthesis.inference: Synthetic data should enter APRL only when functional contact, embodiment correctness, and action effect survive controlled stress.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: August 13 emphasized evidence contracts for adaptation, safety, memory, maps, and generation.
frontier_memory.body: August 14 strengthens the same axis with pre-contact aborts, task-progress probes, active evidence acquisition, and abstention gates.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent editions treated generation mostly as a simulator or stress-input source.
frontier_memory.body: Today adds cross-embodiment manipulation generation as a concrete diagnostic: functional contact and embodiment correctness become first-class metrics.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: Prior VLA notes tracked action routing and adaptation but not ownership of monitor authority.
frontier_memory.body: The current batch still lacks a shared protocol for who can veto the next action: latent world model, activation probe, abstention head, or safety guard.

strategy.title: Pre-commit execution monitor benchmark
strategy.thesis: Benchmark whether latent futures, VLA progress probes, and abstention signals can veto robot actions before irreversible contact or wrong-route commitment.
strategy.one_week: Collect short contact-rich episodes with planned action chunks, residual-stream progress traces, and manually labeled pre-contact failure windows.
strategy.four_week: Compare ContactGuard-style latent futures, task-progress probes, and VLM abstention gates on identical object, viewpoint, and occlusion shifts.
strategy.success: At least one monitor blocks a failing action with usable lead time while keeping false aborts below a predeclared threshold.
strategy.stop: Signals fire only after contact, collapse under unseen objects, or cannot identify which action should be blocked.
strategy.asset: Pre-contact clips, action chunks, latent-future traces, progress-probe logs, abstention labels, and veto outcomes.

strategy.title: Active embodied evidence harness
strategy.thesis: Turn affordance, navigation, and semantic radiance-field tasks into a harness where every extra view must justify a target, route, or interaction change.
strategy.one_week: Create two Habitat or reconstructed scenes with hidden functional cues, ambiguous object labels, and free-space or semantic query logs.
strategy.four_week: Evaluate FUSE-style active views, SAP-Nav hierarchy, SRF simulators, and humanoid VLN routes under occlusion and embodiment constraints.
strategy.success: The harness identifies which observation changed a grounded target, stop decision, route, or contact plan before task success is known.
strategy.stop: Extra views improve confidence text but do not change executable decisions or reduce failure in hidden-cue scenes.
strategy.asset: Viewpoint-action traces, semantic-geometric evidence maps, route decisions, target masks, and embodiment-specific failure labels.

strategy.title: Human-to-robot synthetic data audit
strategy.thesis: Test generated manipulation videos by functional contact and embodiment transfer before using them as robot-training data.
strategy.one_week: Select one handover and one tool-use family, then label task events, contact moments, object responses, and robot embodiment constraints.
strategy.four_week: Compare H2R-Bench dimensions, DreamX-Phi action-conditioned futures, and RGB-D handover generation against downstream policy imitation.
strategy.success: Generated data improves policy behavior only when functional contact and embodiment correctness metrics also improve.
strategy.stop: Video realism increases while contact timing, gripper geometry, or object response stays wrong.
strategy.asset: Human videos, robot embodiment manifests, generated RGB-D clips, contact-transfer labels, and policy-learning deltas.
